findings.source_passage: heedless and reckless as to let go for a moment his one-handed hold... or whether the place where he stood was so treacherous and oozy; or whether the Evil One himself would have it to fall out so, without stating his particular reasons; how it was exactly, there is no telling now
findings.why_it_matters: The source's deliberately uncertain, legally-hedged enumeration of causes ('without stating his particular reasons; how it was exactly, there is no telling now') is a signature voice moment — Ishmael's ironic epistemology in miniature. The draft compresses it to bare alternatives and drops the key closing phrase entirely.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'without stating his particular reasons' and 'how it was exactly, there is no telling now' — these phrases carry the narrator's characteristic mock-judicial voice and should appear verbatim or very close to verbatim.

findings.source_passage: as if that moment seized with some momentous idea; whereas it was only the poor Indian unconsciously revealing by those struggles the perilous depth to which he had sunk
findings.source_locator: paragraph 3, after 'throbbing and heaving just below the surface'
findings.why_it_matters: The aside 'as if that moment seized with some momentous idea' is a characteristically Ishmael-esque satirical deflation — the head appears to think just as it contains a drowning man. The draft retains the bare fact (struggles revealing depth) but strips the ironic simile that gives the passage its voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the clause 'as if that moment seized with some momentous idea' before 'whereas it was only the poor Indian unconsciously revealing' to preserve the rhetorical irony.

findings.source_passage: seemed every instant to be on the point of giving way; an event still more likely from the violent motions of the head
findings.source_locator: paragraph 4, after the hook tears out
findings.why_it_matters: The source specifies that the remaining hook 'seemed every instant to be on the point of giving way' — a prolonged suspension of horror. The draft collapses this to 'strained to part,' losing the sustained tension of that moment.
findings.suggested_fix: Minor: restore 'seemed every instant to be on the point of giving way' to preserve the ticking-clock dread.

findings.source_passage: the exceeding slipperiness of the curb of the Sperm Whale's well
findings.why_it_matters: The draft cuts the comparative rationale ('with much less reason too than the Indian's, considering the exceeding slipperiness of the curb') from the landsmen paragraph, removing a small but characteristic piece of Ishmael's mock-defensive argumentation.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the phrase about 'the exceeding slipperiness of the curb of the Sperm Whale's well' as a subordinate clause to complete the landsmen aside.

summary: The draft is substantially faithful and preserves most major signatures verbatim, but it flattens two characteristically Ishmaelian voice passages — the epistemically hedged accident enumeration and the ironic 'seized with some momentous idea' aside — reducing them to bare fact without the narrator's mock-judicial irony.
